name: Lofoten
tagline: Sea cliffs, low sun, and nobody for miles.
summary: An archipelago that sits above the Arctic Circle and still stays green. Fishing villages on stilts, granite walls straight out of the water, and light that refuses to leave in summer.
alt: A red-roofed house on a rocky shore below snow-covered peaks across Austnesfjorden, Lofoten

name: Alentejo
tagline: Cork oaks, long lunches, and heat that slows you down.
summary: Portugal's quiet interior. Wheat plains, whitewashed hill towns, and a pace that hasn't changed much since the vines went in. The nearest traffic light is usually an hour away.
alt: Two lone trees in an open wheat plain under a pale sky, Alentejo

name: Kii Peninsula
tagline: Cedar forest, pilgrim trails, and river mist at dawn.
summary: South of Osaka the country folds into mountains and stops. Thousand-year pilgrimage routes, hot springs cut into riverbeds, and ryokan where dinner arrives in eleven small dishes.
alt: Forested ridges layered into cloud along the Kumano Kodo, Kii Peninsula

name: Aeolian Islands
tagline: Volcanic rock, caper fields, and boats instead of roads.
summary: Seven islands off Sicily's north coast, most of them without a car worth mentioning. Black sand, white cubic houses, and an active volcano that puts on a show after dark.
alt: The sun setting over the sea behind low island silhouettes, Aeolian Islands

name: Atacama
tagline: The driest place on earth, and the clearest sky above it.
summary: Salt flats, geyser fields, and altitude that makes the horizon feel curved. At night the Milky Way is bright enough to read the ground by.
alt: Eroded rock formations and pale mountains at Catedrales de Tara, Atacama

name: Westfjords
tagline: The part of Iceland the buses never reach.
summary: A fist of land in the northwest, connected by one road that closes when it feels like it. Bird cliffs, hot pots on empty beaches, and roughly seven thousand people in an area the size of Wales.
alt: Dýrafjörður lying mirror-flat between low headlands, Westfjords

name: Kerry
tagline: Weather that changes four times before lunch.
summary: Peninsulas reaching into the Atlantic, stone forts older than most countries, and a coastline that rewards anyone willing to drive slowly with the windows down.
alt: Mist lying across green fields below a dark hill, Dingle Peninsula, Kerry

name: Kalahari
tagline: Red sand, low thorn, and silence with a floor to it.
summary: Not a desert in the empty sense — a semi-arid savanna that turns green after rain and holds some of the last true dark-sky country on the continent.
alt: A giraffe in silhouette against a golden sunrise, Kalahari
